verdict.rationale: Airweave's official MCP server and published skills let off-the-shelf assistants such as Cursor and Claude Code search the same collection of synced data, so several tools can draw on one shared knowledge base. That knowledge comes from synced apps and databases, though, not from what the assistants learn about the user, and nothing shows assistants writing back to it. Missing for 10: assistants writing or updating shared memory about the user, explicit ChatGPT support, and independent hands-on evidence of several assistants sharing one memory.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect off-the-shelf assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) to the same memory so every tool I use shares what it knows about me

citations.quote: The Airweave MCP server implements the Model Context Protocol to let AI assistants search your synced data.

Airweave publishes official skills so that agents in Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and other environments can set up integrations and search your data without you having to explain how every time.
A collection is a group of different data sources that you can search using a single endpoint.
It looks like Airweave works well with Cursor
